agree.reason: Giving the exact Ridgeview cost of about $122 a year and saying the local branch closes in July speaks directly to a fixed-income no-voter, but the 'every vote counts' line in WHY NOW does little to move someone who has already voted no.

honest.reason: Every figure checks out against the brief, and the script rightly leaves out the coffee comparison the brief asked for, which isn't true at the city median of about $6.50 a month; saying the money 'pays for two named things' goes slightly beyond what the brief shows about binding ballot language.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the cost for the Ridgeview median correctly ($121.60 a year, about 33 cents a day), restates the rate as $19 per $100,000 so homeowners can figure their own bill, and uses the 48–52 result to show how close the last vote was.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is stated as the facts show it: without the levy the Ridgeview branch closes in July and Sunday hours stay gone, and the script adds the 22% rise in library visits as the trend.

qualification.reason: The script makes no forecast that needs a hedge, since the six-year end date and the July closure are both stated as plain facts.

objections.reason: It answers 'blank check' with the fixed rate, the six-year limit and the named uses, answers cost by working out the homeowner's own number, and answers 'I voted no last time' with the July closure, all without bringing up the association president or the letter.

fit.reason: The main script runs about 60 to 90 seconds and fits on a card, though the objection lines make one side tight, and the requested coffee line was left out for good reason.
